headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from LightAgent’s MCP/browser/network surface; python-cheatsheet is read-only and non-interactive.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and broad network egress, so attacker-controlled content can plausibly reach its tool-use path. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-interactive, so it is not itself an active injector, but it can still be copied into LightAgent workflows. The pair’s interaction is indirect, so medium fits.
conditions: IF LightAgent ingests content copied from python-cheatsheet into an MCP or browser workflow
IF runtime hooks do not block or sanitize lifecycle payloads
mitigations: Paste only plain text excerpts, not full pages
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to copied content
Use a separate read-only browser profile
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets, while python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, clipboard, or API surfaces and no data classes touched. There is no documented path for python-cheatsheet to receive or exfiltrate LightAgent data, so leakage risk is limited to manual copying of sensitive outputs.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LightAgent outputs into python-cheatsheet notes or issues
IF LightAgent outputs are pasted into a third-party system
mitigations: Keep LightAgent and docs in separate browser profiles
Use a local scratchpad for intermediate notes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and has broad network/MCP capabilities, but python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; only manual coordination mistakes remain.
conditions: IF LightAgent instances are pointed at the same external service account
IF an operator manually routes both agents to the same mutable workspace
mitigations: Do not share a writable workspace
Run only one LightAgent instance per task

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool outputs and workflow state that may be treated as authoritative, while python-cheatsheet is a reference source that could be copied into downstream writing. Because python-cheatsheet is non-executing, the main risk is LightAgent propagating unverified facts into content; the interaction exists but is not directly automated, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LightAgent output is reused as source text without verification
IF a downstream writer treats copied snippets as factual authority

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles secrets and long-term memory, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no declared data classes or residency-sensitive processing. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive LightAgent data in documentation workflows.
conditions: IF LightAgent secrets or user conversations are copied into public documentation
IF retention rules differ in the surrounding operator workflow
mitigations: Keep public docs separate from agent logs
Review retention settings in the host platform
